page: OVHcloud b2-30-flex is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores without multithreading, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on an Intel Haswell-generation processor. The instance provides 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per core, along with 50 GB of local SSD storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses under a KVM hypervisor environment. Acceleration hardware is not included, leaving processing strictly to the host CPU.

Benchmark evaluations reveal an architecture tailored for concurrent execution rather than single-threaded speed. While single-thread benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (917.0) and gzip compression indicate lower-tier throughput due to the older CPU generation and conservative clock speed, multi-core metrics scale efficiently. The instance achieves balanced middle-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (8802.55) and PassMark CPU testing (9398.2), with Redis SET operations sustaining 9.11 million operations per second and static web serving reaching 7.56 GB per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the b2-30-flex delivers predictable dedicated-core capacity and a stable 1:3.75 vCPU-to-memory allocation suitable for standard enterprise tasks. The primary tradeoff lies in the aging Haswell instruction set and constrained single-threaded performance, which makes the instance less viable for intensive real-time compute or large-scale machine learning generation. The profile remains best suited for balanced production workloads, including static and dynamic web serving, Redis caching clusters, CI/CD build environments, and containerized backend microservices.
description: OVHcloud b2-30-flex is a general-purpose virtual server featuring 8 dedicated x86_64 cores clocked at 2.0 GHz on an Intel Haswell architecture, paired with 30.0 GB of memory and 50 GB of local SSD storage. It operates without hardware GPU acceleration under a KVM hypervisor. In benchmark tests, the instance shows balanced multi-core and memory capabilities, delivering 9.11 million Redis SET operations per second and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4607.0, despite weaker single-thread execution rates characteristic of its CPU generation. With 3.75 GB of RAM per dedicated core, it offers balanced resource distribution for non-bursting environments. The server is well positioned for containerized backend services, mid-tier web serving, compilation pipelines, and caching layers that require dedicated compute threads without needing high single-core clocks.
